title: visibility-control.html
content: The Visibility Control feature gives Event Organizers the ability to customize what each {{variable.Object_Attendee}} sees based on their profile, membership status, or role by using the {{variable.Field_Attendee_VisibilityContr}} field on the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} or {{variable.Object_Contact}} record. Use Cases The following are just a few of the ways that you can use Visibility Controls. Use Case 1 Event Organizers can customize Attendees' access to conference tracks or Sessions based on eligibility criteria, ensuring that Attendees only view content relevant to their registration type or interests, thereby enhancing the overall Event experience. Use Case 2 Membership managers can ensure membership exclusivity by making certain Event Items, such as VIP Sessions or special discounts, visible only to paid members. They can tailor the Event experience for members even further by offering exclusive benefits and privileges that incentivize membership and enhance member satisfaction. Use Case 3 Event coordinators can customize the Event experience based on Attendees' roles within an organization or Event, providing personalized experiences that meet an Attendee’s specific needs and preferences. By leveraging Attendee-level controls, Event coordinators can enhance Attendee engagement and satisfaction, ultimately driving Event success. Important to Know When Visibility Controls are set at the {{variable.Object_Event}} level, the preview feature shows the page without enforcing the Visibility Controls. When the Visibility Controls are set at the {{variable.Object_EventItem}} level, the preview feature shows the {{variable.Object_Event}} as if the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} doesn’t have any Visibility Controls assigned. Visibility and the Attendee Record Level You may need to perform additional configuration at the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} record level to ensure the Visibility Controls set on other objects work correctly.  For example, when the {{variable.Field_ETEvent_VisibilityContro}} field is set at the {{variable.Object_Event}} level and an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} 's {{variable.Field_Attendee_VisibilityContr}} field is blank, the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} cannot see their {{variable.AttendeeLink}} . To avoid this issue, the {{variable.Field_Attendee_VisibilityContr}} field must also be set on the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} record.  Since this feature is not automated, users must leverage automation or use List Views to manually set the {{variable.Field_Attendee_VisibilityContr}} field on {{variable.Object_Attendee}} records. Setup The following instructions apply to the {{variable.Object_Event}} , {{variable.Object_EventItem}} , Contact (for {{variable.Feature_ExperienceCloud}} s), {{variable.Object_Attendee}} , and {{variable.Object_Session}} objects. Go to the relevant object. Click the Page Layouts tab. Click the page layout you need to update. Drag and drop the {{variable.Field_Attendee_VisibilityContr}} field on the page layout.  Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . To change the picklist options, click the Fields & Relationships tab. In the Quick Find box, enter and click “Visibility Control.” Scroll to the Values section and edit or create the values. Picklist Values We have provided out-of-the-box values for these Picklist (Multi-Select) fields, but you can also update them with your own values. Attendees Define the {{variable.Field_Attendee_VisibilityContr}} field when you create an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} record.  Event Items When you create an {{variable.Object_EventItem}} , select a value in the {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_VisibilityCo}} field.  You can see five {{variable.Object_EventItem}} s for this {{variable.Object_Event}} , each with its own {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_VisibilityCo}} value. When you add {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s to the {{variable.Object_Event}} , set each {{variable.Object_Attendee}} ’s {{variable.Field_Attendee_VisibilityContr}} field to correlate to the {{variable.Object_EventItem}} (s) they will see in their invite. For example, five {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s have been invited. Two have {{variable.Field_Attendee_VisibilityContr}} = “VIP,” two have {{variable.Field_Attendee_VisibilityContr}} = “Member,” and one has {{variable.Field_Attendee_VisibilityContr}} = “Non-Member.” When you send the invites to these {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s, they will only see the related {{variable.Object_EventItem}} s based on the matched visibility values. For example, an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} with {{variable.Field_Attendee_VisibilityContr}} = “VIP” will see the following {{variable.Object_EventItem}} s. But an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} with {{variable.Field_Attendee_VisibilityContr}} = “Member” will see a different list of {{variable.Object_EventItem}} s. Events Warning If you set the {{variable.Field_ETEvent_VisibilityContro}} at the {{variable.Object_Event}} level and do not set an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} ’s {{variable.Field_Attendee_VisibilityContr}} , the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} cannot see the {{variable.Object_Event}} on their {{variable.AttendeeLink}} . Using the {{variable.Object_EventItem}} example, if we set the {{variable.Object_Event}} ’s {{variable.Field_ETEvent_VisibilityContro}} field to “Member” and “Non-Member,” the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s with {{variable.Field_Attendee_VisibilityContr}} = “VIP” cannot see the {{variable.Object_Event}} . {{variable.Object_Attendee}} {{variable.Field_Attendee_VisibilityContr}} = “Member” {{variable.Object_Attendee}} {{variable.Field_Attendee_VisibilityContr}} = “VIP” Sessions When you create a {{variable.Object_Session}} , select a value in the {{variable.Field_Session_VisibilityContro}} field.  You can see two {{variable.Object_Session}} s for this {{variable.Object_Event}} , each with its own {{variable.Field_Session_VisibilityContro}} value. When you add {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s to the {{variable.Object_Event}} , set each {{variable.Object_Attendee}} ’s {{variable.Field_Attendee_VisibilityContr}} field to correlate to the {{variable.Object_Session}} (s) they will see in their invite. For example, five {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s have been invited. Two have {{variable.Field_Attendee_VisibilityContr}} = “VIP,” two have {{variable.Field_Attendee_VisibilityContr}} = “Member,” and one has {{variable.Field_Attendee_VisibilityContr}} = “Non-Member.” When you send the invites to these {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s, they will only see the related {{variable.Object_Session}} based on the matched visibility values. For example, an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} with {{variable.Field_Attendee_VisibilityContr}} = “VIP” will see the following {{variable.Object_Session}} s. But an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} with {{variable.Field_Attendee_VisibilityContr}} = “Member” will see a different list of {{variable.Object_Session}} s. Visibility and Experience Cloud/Iframes If you need additional functionality, Advanced Visibility , a separate and more complex feature, allows Event Organizers to leverage Contact or Person Account data to restrict visibility within the Experience Cloud or an authenticated iframe. The feature uses rules with specific criteria to determine who can see and register for Events, Event Items, and Sessions. In tandem with Express Registration, Advanced Visibility helps Attendees find and register for relevant Events faster.
